resources.string: Adaptive AOD brightness for crDroid Android 16 on lunaa
Choose Automatic for sensor-based brightness or Manual for one fixed level.
Enabled. AOD brightness follows the selected mode.
Disabled. Stock crDroid AOD brightness is used.
Changes apply on the next AOD activation
Automatic reacts to ambient light. Manual keeps one fixed brightness level.
Current AOD brightness: waiting for sensor…
Stock crDroid AOD brightness is active
Extra Bright %1$s · %2$d%% · available in strong daylight
Extra Bright %1$s · %2$d%% requested for this AOD session
Pick a fixed profile. Balanced uses the full normal AOD range; Bright Daylight can add Extra Bright in strong daylight.
Softest automatic profile for dark rooms and night use.
Recommended everyday profile using the full normal AOD brightness range without HBM.
Bright Daylight uses the full normal range and can add Extra Bright above the daylight threshold.
Bright Daylight can use Extra Bright in strong daylight. Turn it off below to keep the bright curve without HBM.
Extra Bright is off. Bright Daylight stays on the normal AOD brightness curve without HBM.
Uses one fixed AOD level and ignores ambient light.
Choose Dim, Balanced or Bright. Bright is 100% normal AOD brightness; Extra Bright is controlled separately.
Extra Bright is off. Manual Bright stays at 100% normal AOD brightness.
Choose Low, Medium or Max HBM strength. Manual Bright and Bright Daylight each have their own Extra Bright toggle.
Low is softer and Max is full fingerprint-HBM. Exact percentages are available in Advanced settings.
Set the exact percentage behind each named brightness level. Values must stay between 1 and 100 and increase from left to right.
Enter a value from 1 to 100 for every level.
Manual must be Dim ≤ Balanced ≤ Bright and Extra Bright must be Low ≤ Medium ≤ Max.
Defaults restored in the form. Tap Save changes to apply them.
Preset changed. Tap Save changes to apply it.
Settings cannot be exposed to Vector/Xposed on this build; Save changes is disabled.
Saved. Changes apply on the next AOD activation.
Very high manual AOD brightness can use more power.
